messages:
elena: Heads-up — I pushed RBAC refactor r4321 to staging this morning. After the smoke tests some private control-plane admin flows for on-prem tenants started failing. Not a full lockout but cannot list KMS keys or read audit configs.
cheng: Same here in dedicated-staging-1. Control-plane logs show `AccessDenied: kms:Decrypt` and `permission denied: iam.roles.get`.
deploy-bot: rollout r4321 -> staging completed at 2026-06-02T08:12:34Z :white_check_mark:
nana: Quick Q — did the refactor change any SA->role bindings used by private control-plane services? I noticed a note about moving to namespaced bindings.
mike: The new binding set includes a condition like:
```
bindings:
  - role: roles/redwood.controlplaneAdmin
    members:
      - serviceAccount:controlplane:cp-sa
    condition:
      expression: "resource.project == request.auth.claims.project"
```
That condition blocks cross-project operations (our on-prem proxies operate across project boundaries).
elena: Right. Our tenant KMS keys live in a different project; the condition prevents cp-sa from decrypting tenant keys.
cheng: Short-term options: add an explicit KMS binding allowing cp-sa kms:Decrypt on affected keys OR roll back r4321 in staging (and delay prod rollout).
jules: Proposing emergency patch: reintroduce a temporary legacy binding `roles/redwood.controlplaneAdmin:legacy` scoped to specific tenant keys with an annotation `temp:rbac-hotfix` and a 48h TTL, then monitor.
security-eng: +1 for hotfix but must be auditable. If we add temporary binding, log the change and create an automated eval to detect regressions within 24h.
nana: Also validate VPC allowlist/source condition changes — the refactor may have tightened source constraints and caused signed-token checks to fail for some admin consoles.
mike: I ran this in staging to confirm the denial:
```
gcloud kms keys list --project=tenant-42
```
Result: PERMISSION_DENIED for cp-sa. Stack trace points to controlplane/key-unwrapper.go:72.
elena: Mitigation checklist: 
- add temp binding for cp-sa -> kms:Decrypt on affected tenant key(s)
- create alert: `AccessDenied: kms:Decrypt` spike (>5 / 1m)
- rollback r4321 if hotfix doesn't resolve all issues
- postmortem and update RBAC migration docs
cheng: Applying binding in staging now:
```
gcloud kms keys add-iam-policy-binding projects/tenant-42/locations/global/keyRings/rw/cryptoKeys/tenant-key \
  --member="serviceAccount:controlplane@staging.redwood-inference.iam.gserviceaccount.com" \
  --role="roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyDecrypter"
```
cheng: After binding, re-ran bootstrap/admin smoke tests — audit-configs: OK, key unwrap: OK.
security-eng: Opening incident INC-2026-049 and linking PR r4321. Tagging infra and compliance. We need to audit KMS policies for all on-prem tenants and add RBAC unit tests to CI that simulate cross-project unwraps.
mike: I've assigned reviewers in the ticket: @security-eng, @sre-oncall.
jules: Longer-term fix: migration should create scoped fallback bindings before removing broad roles. Add a `migration:grace-period` TTL tag so ops can revoke after validation window.
nana: Also confirm audit logs include `iam.setPolicy` entries and the actor identity. We saw an opaque CI service account execute the change in staging.
elena: Deploy tool likely made the change via CI service account — ensure it has limited scope and KMS ACLs are explicit.
security-eng: I'll lead the postmortem and schedule a 1h blameless RCA tomorrow. Action items assigned in INC-2026-049.
mike: Creating regression ticket to add a CI test case that simulates cross-project key unwraps and checks `kms:Decrypt` success.
elena: Closing the thread for now — applying hotfix in prod if staging mirrors, monitoring alerts, and will update the incident with timeline. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
